newsitem.title: USA: Georgia economic indicators turn downward in March.
newsitem.headline: Georgia economic indicators turn downward in March.

text.p: Georgia's Composite Index of Leading Economic Indicators turned downward in March for the second time in three months, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said in his monthly report.
Leading indicators, designed to predict economic activity three to six months ahead, declined 0.27 point to 147.02 on a 1988 base of 100.
The Composite Index of Coincident Indicators, designed to measure current economic activity, rose 0.29 point to 145.35 on a 1987 base of 100.
Forecasts have been that the state's robust economy, which has slowed since the 1996 Summer Olympic Games, will continue to grow through 1997 but at a less dramatic pace.

Downward pressure on the index of leading indicators in March came from increases in initial jobless claims, a decline in the number of manufacturing workers and a drop in applications for new corporate charters.
On the upside, the state saw increases in titles issued for new motor vehicles, residential building permits and the number of hours worked by manufacturing employees.
The average manufacturing work week increased 18 mintues to 42.6 hours in March. That suggests total manufacturing employment, which decreased 500 to 588,400 in March, may turn around in April.
The state issued 38,008 titles for new motor vehicles in March, up 6.84 percent over February. Residential building permits rose by 7.84 percent to 6,024 in March.
Total nonfaram employment increased by 1,000 to 3.57 million in March.

State revenue collections increased by 0.47 percent to $873.6 million in March Sales tax receipts, which had been on the downswing since an October reduction in the levy on groceries, rebounded to $349 million, a 1.46 percent increase over February.
Averge weekly manufacturing earnings rose $5.41 to $490.85 in March, partly due to increasing overtime hours. That was down $5.04 from last March.
Georgia's unemployment rate held steady at 4.7 percent in March, unchanged from February and up from 4.6 percent a year ago.
Initial jobless claims rose to 27,745 in March, a 7.13 percent increase over February. Continued claims rose 7.06 percent, to 182,634.
Applications for new corporate charters dipped 3.46 percent in March to 2,912.
